title: What the literature knows
summary: A structured review of what GCAM and other integrated assessment models say about decarbonising transport: foundations, model comparisons, applications by mode and fuel, and Saudi Arabia.
outcomes: Place a transport research question within four strands of GCAM literature
Summarise what model comparisons say about why IAMs disagree on transport
Identify what is known, what is disputed and what is still unknown
Find the Saudi Arabia and downscaling studies that a regional study must cite
narration_en: Before you design a study, find out what is already known. This module organises the GCAM transport literature into four strands. The first is foundations: the papers that built GCAM's transport sector, including the University of California Davis database and early work on vehicle technologies. The second is model comparison: studies that ran several integrated assessment models on the same question and found that they disagree, mostly because of different assumptions about behaviour, costs and demand, not because of different maths. The third is applications: electric vehicles, hydrogen, biofuels for aviation, freight, and country studies. The fourth is Saudi Arabia and downscaling: the GCAM-KSA model, which separates Saudi Arabia from the Middle East region, and methods for taking regional results down to countries. The module ends with a synthesis of what is agreed, what is disputed and what remains unknown. Most links have been checked; a few details are marked as unverified, and you should check them before you cite.
narration_ar: قبل أن تصمم دراستك، اعرف ما هو معروف بالفعل. تنظّم هذه الوحدة أدبيات النقل في نموذج GCAM في أربعة مسارات. الأول هو الأسس: الأوراق التي بنت قطاع النقل في النموذج، ومنها قاعدة بيانات جامعة كاليفورنيا في ديفيس والأعمال المبكرة عن تقنيات المركبات. والثاني هو مقارنة النماذج: دراسات شغّلت عدة نماذج للتقييم المتكامل على السؤال نفسه فوجدت أنها تختلف، ويرجع ذلك في الغالب إلى اختلاف الافتراضات حول السلوك والتكاليف والطلب، لا إلى اختلاف الرياضيات. والثالث هو التطبيقات: المركبات الكهربائية والهيدروجين والوقود الحيوي للطيران والشحن والدراسات القُطرية. والرابع هو المملكة العربية السعودية وتقليص المقياس: نموذج GCAM-KSA الذي يفصل المملكة عن منطقة الشرق الأوسط، وطرق نقل النتائج الإقليمية إلى مستوى الدول. وتختتم الوحدة بخلاصة لما هو متفق عليه وما هو مختلف فيه وما يبقى مجهولًا. وقد جرى التحقق من معظم الروابط، وبعض التفاصيل موسومة بأنها غير متحقق منها، فتحقق منها قبل أن تستشهد بها.

diagram.title: The GCAM transport literature in four strands
diagram.caption: Every strand feeds the synthesis; your question should start from its gaps.

nodes.label: GCAM transport literature
nodes.detail: About 33 peer-reviewed studies and grey literature collected for this course; DOIs checked where possible.

nodes.label: Foundations
nodes.detail: UC Davis database, Kyle and Kim (2011) on light-duty vehicles, GCAM model descriptions and gcamdata.

nodes.label: Model comparisons
nodes.detail: Edelenbosch et al. (2017) and related studies: decomposing passenger futures across IAMs; behaviour and demand assumptions dominate.

nodes.label: Applications
nodes.detail: Electric vehicles, hydrogen, biojet fuels for aviation, freight, zero-emission transport (Speizer et al., 2024), USA, China, India.

nodes.label: Saudi Arabia, downscaling
nodes.detail: GCAM-KSA papers (2024–2025), KAPSARC transport studies with 2060 results, and DSCALE (Sferra et al., 2026).

nodes.label: Synthesis
nodes.detail: Agreed: electrification dominates light-duty decarbonisation. Disputed: speed of uptake, role of hydrogen and biofuels. Unknown: behaviour, freight and aviation fuels at scale.

tour.text: Start with the foundations: how GCAM's transport sector and data were built.
Model comparisons show why IAMs disagree: assumptions about behaviour, cost and demand.
Applications test technologies, fuels and policies by mode and by country.
Saudi Arabia and downscaling: GCAM-KSA and methods to reach country level.
Read the synthesis last: the gaps there are where new research is needed.

sections.heading: How this review was built
sections.html: The list was compiled on 23 October 2026 from journal searches, PNNL/OSTI records, JGCRI model proposals and the KAPSARC publication pages. Each DOI below was checked against a publisher, PNNL, OSTI, IDEAS or Semantic Scholar record. Items whose DOI, pages or model list could not be confirmed are marked [U]. Read the papers themselves before citing a finding; the one-line summaries here are a map, not a substitute.

sections.html:
Known (several studies agree)Disputed (results depend on model or assumption)Unknown or barely studied
  • Transport cuts lag power and buildings at the same carbon price
  • In IAMs, cuts come mostly from vehicle efficiency and fuel switching
  • Freight and aviation are the hardest residuals

  • How much travel and mode shift policy can deliver (models vs sectoral studies)

callouts.title: Why this matters
callouts.html: When eight global models were run with the same climate policy, almost all of the passenger-transport emission cuts came from cleaner fuels and more efficient vehicles; travelling less or switching to rail barely registered (Edelenbosch et al. 2017). Is that a fact about the world, or about how the models were built? That question runs through this whole module.

callouts.title: Research note
callouts.html: Reading a model-comparison paper. Ask four questions: (1) Were the scenarios harmonised in GDP, population and policy, or only in name? (2) Which differences come from base-year data (Yeh et al. 2017 found these large) and which from structure? (3) Does the decomposition method (Laspeyres, LMDI) leave a residual? (4) Which options could a model not choose because it does not contain them? The last one is why "little mode shift" can be a structural result rather than an empirical one.

callouts.title: Pitfall
callouts.html: Citing a finding without its version. Kyle & Kim (2011) used a GCAM with different technologies, costs and share-weight paths from today's v9.1; the GCAM-KSA papers use GCAM 6.0 with a 2015 base year. A finding is a statement about a model version under stated assumptions. Report it that way, and do not compare numbers across versions without saying so.

callouts.title: Try it
callouts.html:
1. Pick one study from Theme C. Write its research question as a single decision someone could take, and name the output variable that answers it.
  2. Which two studies would you put side by side to argue that GCAM under-states mode shift? What evidence would change your mind?

takeaways: Read the four strands before choosing a question: foundations, comparisons, applications, Saudi Arabia and downscaling
Models disagree mainly through assumptions on behaviour, costs and demand
Electrification of light vehicles is the most robust finding; aviation, shipping and freight fuels are the least settled
Check every DOI and detail marked unverified before citing it

quiz.q: According to model-comparison studies, IAMs disagree on transport mainly because of…
options: Different assumptions about behaviour, costs and demand
quiz.explain: Comparisons trace most of the spread to input and behavioural assumptions.

quiz.q: What does GCAM-KSA change compared with the public GCAM release?
options: It separates Saudi Arabia from the Middle East region
quiz.explain: GCAM-KSA (built on GCAM 6.0) models Saudi Arabia as its own region.

quiz.q: Which transport segment is least settled in the literature?
quiz.explain: Fuels for long-haul aviation and shipping remain the most disputed.
Sferra et al. (2026) describe DSCALE for downscaling regional and global pathways to country level.

explorer.intro: Two toy models, one carbon price. Change one model's solar cost or demand response and watch how far their 2050 emissions move apart.
explorer.predict: Which assumption do you think moves the answer more: technology cost or how strongly people cut demand when prices rise?
